summary: Comprehensive testing of eKlaim Lyra MVP (both backend + frontend). Backend: 20/20 pytest cases pass covering setup/auth/roles, users, categories, file upload (jpg/png+bad-ext), OCR fallback, full claim workflow (draft -> submit -> verify -> approve -> pay with proof + petty-cash debit), top-up workflow (verifikator request -> finance approve -> petty-cash credit), reconciliation balanced, dashboard shape, audit-trail RBAC, reports. Frontend: login page renders corporate blue split screen, admin login works, all navigable routes render (dashboard, klaim/baru, klaim-saya, petty-cash, top-up, verifikasi, approval, pembayaran, pengguna, kategori, rekonsiliasi, audit-trail, laporan). Dashboard shows KPI cards (saldo Rp 5.850.000, 117% dari saldo awal), action queue cards, tren pengeluaran chart & top kategori chart, recent claims. Petty Cash page shows balance, riwayat mutasi, Request Top-up button. Laporan shows filter + summary cards + CSV export button. Fixed 1 real React bug encountered on 5 pages (see updated_files).

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught runtime error 'destroy is not a function' - useEffect(load, []) where load returns a Promise. FIXED by wrapping in arrow: useEffect(() => { load(); }, [])

issues: Uses native browser date picker (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of shadcn/ui Calendar component. Locale is en-US so users see mm/dd/yyyy which is confusing for Bahasa Indonesia UI (should be dd/MM/yyyy).

'117% dari saldo awal' label when saldo_sekarang > saldo_awal after top-up is slightly misleading (implies over-limit). Consider showing absolute delta instead of percentage of saldo_awal, or cap the progress bar at 100%.
After successful login the app navigates to '/' (root) rather than '/dashboard'; dashboard component still renders at '/' so functional, but slightly inconsistent with route naming.

action_items: Consider replacing native <input type=date> with shadcn Calendar/Popover DatePicker to match corporate design language and use dd/MM/yyyy Indonesian format.
Review the '117% dari saldo awal' UX (cap the progress bar or reword when balance > initial after top-up).
Optional: on Login success push('/dashboard') instead of '/' for URL clarity.
Nice-to-have: add data-testid attributes on dashboard KPI cards ('kpi-petty-cash', 'kpi-total-klaim', 'kpi-total-dibayar') and action queue cards for easier automated regression testing.
critical_code_review_comments: useEffect(load, []) anti-pattern was present on 5 pages - React saw the returned Promise as a cleanup function and threw TypeError on unmount. Always wrap: useEffect(() => { load(); }, []) or make load a useCallback. Consider ESLint rule react-hooks/exhaustive-deps.
server.py reconciliation endpoint has commented-out dead code and duplicate 'expected =' calculation (lines 783-788). Should be cleaned up.

OCR endpoint catches all exceptions and returns 200 with 'catatan': f'OCR gagal: {e}'. Good for UX resilience but should also log at ERROR level with request_id/user_id for observability (currently uses logger.exception which is fine).
File upload MIME_TYPES accepts 'gif' but /api/ocr/receipt rejects non-image content_type only by prefix (fine). PDF upload allowed but OCR silently returns empty - good.
/api/setup/init password 'admin123' is hard-coded and returned in response body. Fine for MVP bootstrap; ensure production forces a password reset on first login.
server.py is 878 lines in a single file - consider splitting into routers/ (auth, users, claims, topups, files, ocr, dashboard, reports) as it grows.

petty_cash IN/OUT transactions and claim payment are not wrapped in a MongoDB transaction - a crash between apply_petty_cash and claim status update could produce inconsistent state. For MVP acceptable but should be documented.
JWT_SECRET has a default fallback 'eklaim-lyra-secret-change-me'. Should raise if not set in production env (per env-var-first rule).

rca of the issue: React error 'destroy is not a function' RCA: The pattern useEffect(load, []) passes load directly as the effect. Because load is defined as () => api.get(...).then(setData), it returns a Promise. React expects the return value of an effect to be either undefined or a cleanup function; when it later attempts to invoke the returned Promise as a cleanup, it fails with TypeError. Reproduction: navigate to /petty-cash, /pengguna, /kategori, /top-up, or /klaim-saya - runtime error overlay appears. Mitigation applied: wrap invocation - useEffect(() => { load(); }, []) - so the effect returns undefined. Verified all 5 pages now render cleanly with no page errors.
